b: I’ve been working on launching a men’s skincare brand, and I’m starting to question whether my branding strategy is a contradiction.

The product is a $38 skin balm made with premium, predominantly naturally derived ingredients, with grass-fed beef tallow as the primary ingredient.
But the branding is anything but traditional premium skincare.

I created a fictional 1980s stuntman named Jack Holt. The brand is built around ridiculous masculinity (think Commando, Predator, Rambo, etc), motorcycles, wrestling, fake inventions (combat knife with balm in handle, caulk gun balm applicator, bandolier with grenade and skin balm compartments), and over-the-top humor.
Think Old Spice’s personality applied to a premium skincare product.
My thinking was that premium skincare products are often fantastic, but so much of the branding feels interchangeable. Minimalist packaging, muted colors, clinical messaging, etc.
I wanted to build something that was genuinely entertaining and different without compromising on the actual product.

But here’s my concern:
Does humor undermine perceived quality when you’re asking someone to spend $38 on a moisturizer?
Can a brand be ridiculous while its product is taken seriously?
I’m especially curious how others would approach balancing product credibility with an intentionally absurd brand identity.
